overview.text:
Majuli, in the Brahmaputra, is recognised by Guinness as the world's largest inland river island, though erosion had shrunk it to about 880 sq km by 2024. Since Sankardev founded satras here in the 16th century it has been the centre of Assam's Vaishnavite culture: Dakhinpat, Kamalabari, Auniati with its Sattriya dance, and Samaguri, famous for bamboo-and-wood masks.

The Misings are the largest community, alongside Deoris and Sonowal-Kacharis, and their food — fish steamed in leaves, bamboo-roasted chicken, massing chutney — is reason enough to stay. November is the time to come, for the Raas Mahotsav and cool weather. Majuli is reached by ferry from Nimati Ghat near Jorhat, about 250 km from Guwahati; a road bridge is being built.
